world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Some other tips on pronunciation. Most Nukunu words carry the stress on the first syllable of the word. The ‘stressed’ part of the word is in bold in these examples: wakarra back of neck; ngatyu my; maṛa hand
new_statements.citation: Mobile Language Team (University of Adelaide) with the Nukunu community. n.d. [c. 2020]. Nukunu Lesson 2: Sounds and Spelling. Online Language Learning Portal, https://portal.mobilelanguageteam.com.au/lessons/nukunu-lesson-2/ (accessed 2026-09-17).
new_statements.locator: section 'Some other tips on pronunciation' (end of lesson, after the consonant list)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word (bold in the source on wa-karra, nga-tyu, ma-ṛa).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned. (For comparison, Hercus 1999:35 gives Wirangu, a neighbouring Thura-Yura language, initial stress 'as is the case in all the surrounding languages' with secondary stress on the third syllable of longer words; and Eira 2010:39 cites Hercus 1992 as supporting first-syllable stress in related languages.)
new_statements.exceptions: 'Most' words — implies unspecified exceptions; none listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; illustrated with isolated citation forms (nouns/pronouns). Community language-learning lesson in the modern Nukunu orthography, built on Hercus 1992 (the companion wordlist page says its words come from that dictionary).
new_statements.identity_note: Nukunu = Nugunu (Australia), glottocode nugu1241, ISO nnv; Thura-Yura, Pama-Nyungan; southern Flinders Ranges / Port Augusta, SA. The MLT lesson describes the revived modern Nukunu variety (orthography of the Nukunu Wapma Thura / Mobile Language Team programme) built on Hercus 1992's salvage record; same languoid, no dialect distinction. Not to be confused with Nugunu (Cameroon), nugu1242. Note that the Glottolog descriptive reference attached to nugu1241 in our WORLD_TARGETS extract (Sun 2015, Sastod Rgyalrong) is a mismatch; Glottolog's actual meds are Hercus 1992 (51 pp.), Black 1917 and Valentine 1886.
